problems.title: Grade bands with validity
problems.statement: Read one integer score. If it is below 0 or above 100 print INVALID. Otherwise print the letter grade: A for 90 and up, B for 80 and up, C for 70 and up, D for 60 and up, F otherwise.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: A starts at 90 but the student used a strict comparison, so 90 gets a B.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Wrote = instead of a comparison for the B band, so every score below 90 gets B.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Forgot the invalid-score case entirely.

problems.title: Leap years in a list
problems.statement: Read n, then n years. Print how many of them are leap years, then on the next line print the last leap year in the list, or NONE if there is none.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Used = in the divisible-by-4 test, which sets r to 0 and makes the condition false.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Joined the century rule with && instead of ||, so ordinary leap years fail.

bugs.label: CPP_STALE_EXIT
bugs.note: Keeps the first leap year found instead of the last one.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Forgot the divisible-by-400 exception, so years like 2000 are not leap.

problems.title: Triangle type
problems.statement: Read three positive side lengths (they can be as large as 1500000000). Print INVALID if they cannot form a triangle (a degenerate one with two sides summing to the third also counts as invalid), otherwise EQUILATERAL, ISOSCELES or SCALENE.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Used < instead of <= for the first side pair, so a degenerate triangle slips through.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Wrote = instead of == in the equilateral test, which overwrites a.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Isosceles test forgets to compare the first and third sides.

bugs.label: CPP_INT_OVERFLOW
bugs.note: Sum of two large sides overflows int, so valid triangles look invalid.

problems.title: FizzBuzz
problems.statement: Read n. For each i from 1 to n print on its own line FizzBuzz if i is divisible by 3 and 5, Fizz if divisible by 3, Buzz if divisible by 5, otherwise i itself.

bugs.label: CPP_LOOP_BOUNDARY
bugs.note: Loop stops one short because of < instead of <=.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Wrote = in the Buzz test so it is never true.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Used || for the FizzBuzz test, so multiples of 3 or 5 all print FizzBuzz.

bugs.label: CPP_OFF_BY_ONE
bugs.note: Starts counting at 0 so an extra line for 0 is printed.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Misspelled the FizzBuzz output text.

problems.title: In-range count and longest run
problems.statement: Read n, a lower bound lo and an upper bound hi, then n integers. Print the number of values with lo <= x <= hi, then the length of the longest block of consecutive in-range values, separated by a space.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Bounds are inclusive but the student excluded both ends.

bugs.label: CPP_STALE_EXIT
bugs.note: The current run counter is never reset when an out-of-range value appears.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Stores the latest run instead of the longest run.

problems.title: Signs and product sign
problems.statement: Read n then n integers. Print the count of negatives, zeros and positives separated by spaces. On the next line print the sign of the product of all the numbers (ZERO, POSITIVE or NEGATIVE) without multiplying them.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Used = in the zero test, so zeros are counted as positive.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Zero is included in the negative test.

bugs.label: CPP_STALE_EXIT
bugs.note: Stops reading numbers at the first zero, so later values are never counted.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Wrong parity test for the product sign.

problems.title: Date validity
problems.statement: Read day, month and year (year at least 1). Print VALID if it is a real calendar date (leap years follow the Gregorian rule), otherwise INVALID.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Rejects the last day of every month.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Wrote = in the February test, which overwrites the month.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Leap-year rule misses years divisible by 400.

problems.title: Progressive tax
problems.statement: Read an income (integer, up to 2000000000). Tax is 10 percent of the first 10000, 20 percent of the part between 10000 and 40000, and 30 percent of the part above 40000. Compute each portion with integer division by 100 and print the total tax.

bugs.label: CPP_INT_OVERFLOW
bugs.note: The portion times 30 overflows int for large incomes.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Compared against the wrong bound for the top bracket.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Forgot to cut the income down after taxing the top bracket, so it is taxed again.

problems.title: Parking fee
problems.statement: Read the minutes parked m. The first 30 minutes of each day are free; after that each started hour costs 2, but a single day (1440 minutes) never costs more than 20. Every full 1440 minutes costs exactly 20. Print the total fee.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Compared against the wrong bound for the free period.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Used = in the zero check, which sets m to 0.

bugs.label: CPP_OFF_BY_ONE
bugs.note: Rounding up to started hours is off by one.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Forgot the daily cap.

problems.title: Voting eligibility
problems.statement: Read n people. For each, read age, citizen (1 or 0) and registered (1 or 0). A person is eligible if age is at least 18 and both flags are 1. Print the number of eligible people and the age of the youngest eligible person (or -1 if none), separated by a space.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Voting age is 18 but the student used a strict comparison.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Wrote = in the citizen check, which overwrites the flag and is always true.

bugs.label: CPP_STALE_EXIT
bugs.note: Keeps the first eligible age forever instead of updating the minimum.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Comparison direction finds the oldest, not the youngest.

problems.title: Numeric password rules
problems.statement: Read a positive integer (up to 18 digits). It is a VALID password if it has between 6 and 10 digits, no two neighbouring digits are equal, and its digit sum is at least 20. Otherwise print INVALID.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Chained comparison is always true, so the length is never checked.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Wrote = in the final condition, which makes it always false.

bugs.label: CPP_STALE_EXIT
bugs.note: The previous digit is never updated, so repeats are not noticed.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Adds 1 per digit instead of the digit value.

problems.title: Cinema ticket total
problems.statement: Read n and the weekday number (1 to 7), then n ages. Under 3 is free, 3 to 12 costs 8, 13 to 64 costs 12, 65 and over costs 9. On weekday 2 every non-free ticket is 2 cheaper. Print the total.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Child band should include age 12.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Wrote = for the weekday test, so the day variable is overwritten.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Discount is also applied to free tickets, giving negative prices.

problems.title: Freezing and heat readings
problems.statement: Read n temperature readings. Print the 1-based position of the first reading below 0 and the position of the last reading above 30, separated by a space. Use -1 for a missing one.

bugs.label: CPP_STALE_EXIT
bugs.note: Keeps the first hot reading instead of the last one.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Reading of exactly 30 is counted as above 30.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Wrote = so first is overwritten on every reading.

bugs.label: CPP_OFF_BY_ONE
bugs.note: Reports 0-based positions instead of 1-based.

problems.title: Part of the day
problems.statement: Read hour h and minute m. If h is not 0-23 or m not 0-59 print INVALID. Otherwise print MORNING (5:00-11:59), AFTERNOON (12:00-16:59), EVENING (17:00-20:59) or NIGHT, followed by the word SHARP (after a space) when m is 0.

bugs.label: CPP_RANGE_CHECK
bugs.note: Noon is excluded from the afternoon band.

bugs.label: CPP_ASSIGN_VS_COMPARE
bugs.note: Wrote = in the SHARP test, so SHARP is never printed.

bugs.label: CPP_OTHER_ERROR
bugs.note: Forgot to reject minutes above 59.
